paragraphs: The XJ8 was a key part of Jaguar's XJ range through the late 1990s and 2000s, offering V8 power in a more accessible package than the supercharged XJR. It used the naturally aspirated AJ-V8 engine across two generations — the X308 (1997–2003) and the X350 (2002–2009) — with capacities ranging from 3.2 litres to 4.0 litres depending on the market and specification. The AJ-V8 was Jaguar's first all-new V8 design, and while it's a robust engine overall, timing chain components and valve seals are common service items at higher mileage. The XJ8 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road. Jaguar XJ8 Engine Codes AJ-V8 (X308, X350) A naturally aspirated V8 fitted to the XJ8 from 1997 to 2009 across two generations. The X308 generation used the 3.2-litre and 4.0-litre versions of the AJ-V8, while the later X350 generation continued with the 4.0-litre AJ-V8 before being replaced by the 4.2-litre unit in some markets. We replace timing chains, tensioners, valve seals and gaskets as standard on every AJ-V8 rebuild. cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the XJ8 from 2023 to present. The AJ-V8 (naturally aspirated) features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older AJ-V8 (naturally aspirated) V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every AJ-V8 (naturally aspirated) rebuild.
